problems.title: Mean of inserted arithmetic terms
problems.question: Seven numbers are inserted between1 and2 to form an arithmetic progression. Find the mean of the inserted numbers.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The progression has9 terms and common difference(2−1)/8=1/8.
steps: The first and last inserted terms are9/8 and15/8.
Their mean,and therefore the mean of the seven arithmetic terms,is(9/8+15/8)/2.

problems.title: Two rays in a regular octagon
problems.question: In regular octagon ABCDEFGH,rays DB and FA meet at P. Find angle APB.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Each minor side arc is45°. Chord DB has midpoint-arc direction through C,and is perpendicular to radius OC.
steps: Using vertex arguments0°,45°,90°,…,line DB is horizontal,while line FA has inclination22.5° to it.
The intersection on the specified rays gives the acute angle22.5°.

problems.title: Collinearity and a distance ratio
problems.question: O=(0,0),A=(2,3),B=(2x−1,x) are collinear. Find OB/OA.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Their coordinate determinant is2x−3(2x−1)=0.
steps: Distances from the origin scale by the absolute multiplier.

problems.title: Larger side from parallelogram diagonals
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals10,12 with angle30°. Find its larger side.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Side vectors are half the sum and half the difference of the diagonal vectors.

problems.title: Area of an annulus from a tangent chord
problems.question: An outer-circle chord of length6 cm touches the concentric inner circle. Find annulus area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Half-chord3,radii R,r satisfy R²=r²+3².

problems.title: A perpendicular vector combination
problems.question: a=(0,1),b=(1,2). Find m with a⊥(a−mb).
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: a−mb=(−m,1−2m); perpendicularity means dot product0.

problems.title: Circumcircle area from an arithmetic angle progression
problems.question: A triangle’s angles form an arithmetic progression. Its middle-length side is15 cm. Find circumcircle area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The middle angle is180°/3=60°. The middle side lies opposite it.

problems.title: An arithmetic partial sum from a symmetric pair
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₇+a₁₂=11. Find S₁₈.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Since7+12=1+18,the pair sums a₇+a₁₂ and a₁+a₁₈ are equal.

problems.title: A squared root and an absolute value
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt{2-x})^2-\sqrt{x^2-6x+9}$.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The first square root requires x≤2; the second root is|x−3|.
problems.note: The small superscript2 in the source belongs outside the first radical;reading it as√(2−x²) changes the question.

problems.title: A parameter for collinear vectors
problems.question: For which k are a=(−3,k),b=(k,−1) collinear?
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The determinant must vanish:(−3)(−1)−k²=0.
steps: k²=3. Both signs give valid nonzero collinear vectors.

problems.title: A symmetric expression in quadratic roots
problems.question: Roots x₁,x₂ satisfy3x²−5x−4=0. Find x₁²−x₁x₂+x₂².
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Vieta:x₁+x₂=5/3,x₁x₂=−4/3; expression=(sum)²−3product.

problems.title: Recover a term from partial sums
problems.question: Sₙ=1.5n²−3.5n. Find the third arithmetic term.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: a₃=S₃−S₂.

problems.title: A triangle side equal to its circumradius
problems.question: Two sides are6 and8;the third side equals circumradius R. Find the area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: By the sine rule,third side=2RsinC=R,so sinC=1/2.
steps: Whether C is30° or150°,the area is(1/2)·6·8sinC.

problems.title: An internal common tangent length
problems.question: Two disjoint circles have radii2,4 and center distance10. A common tangent has the centers on opposite sides. Find the distance between tangency points.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Internal tangent length²=d²−(r₁+r₂)².

problems.title: Find an excised sector angle
problems.question: A radius6 disk has a sector removed;remaining area is33π cm². Find the sector angle.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Full area=36π,removed area=3π.
steps: The sector is3π/(36π)=1/12 of the disk.

problems.title: Only the middle gaps are shaded
problems.question: Two radius1 circles touch inside a rectangle,as in the source figure. Find the shaded top and bottom middle gaps.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The central rectangle between the two circle centers has width2,height2,area4.
steps: Inside that rectangle,the circles contribute two semicircles,total areaπ.
The shaded middle gaps are the complement;the four outer corner gaps are not shaded.

problems.title: Recognize an odd function
problems.question: Which listed function is odd:x+10,x²−5,x³+x,or1/(x+3)?
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Odd means f(−x)=−f(x) on a symmetric domain.
steps: The constants or shifted denominator prevent the other choices from having this symmetry.

problems.title: A midpoint line cuts a square diagonal
problems.question: A square has diagonal2. E is midpoint of BC;ED meets AC at F. Find AF.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
steps: ED has equation y=1−x/2;AC has y=x. Their intersection has x=y=2/3.

problems.title: Area enclosed by a circle equation
problems.question: Find the area bounded by x²−4x+y²=0.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Complete the square:(x−2)²+y²=4.
steps: This is a circle of radius2.

problems.title: Travel times after a meeting
problems.question: Two cars leave opposite ends simultaneously toward each other. After meeting,the first takes16 hours to the far end and the second25 hours. Find their total times.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: If t is the time before meeting,then t²=16·25 by equal-distance speed ratios.
steps: For speeds u,v,the equations ut=25v and vt=16u multiply to t²=400.
Thus t=20. Add the remaining times.

problems.title: A circular segment of angle120 degrees
problems.question: A segment has chord6 cm and minor arc120°. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Chord=2Rsin60°=√3R,so R=2√3. Segment=sector minus isosceles triangle.

problems.title: A vector from a rhombus center
problems.question: O is the diagonal intersection of rhombus ABCD. M∈AD with AM:MD=1:2. Express OM using AB and AD.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Take A as origin,u=AB,v=AD. Then O=(u+v)/2,M=v/3.

problems.title: An octagon and triangle on the same circle
problems.question: A regular octagon inscribed in a circle has area16√6. Find the inscribed equilateral triangle’s area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Octagon area=2√2R²;equilateral triangle area=3√3R²/4.

problems.title: Increasing interval of a cube root
problems.question: Find the increasing interval of y=∛(x−2)+3.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The cube-root function is strictly increasing on all real numbers;translations preserve this.
steps: Every pair x₁<x₂ has x₁−2<x₂−2,and cube roots preserve the inequality.

problems.title: Two reciprocal cubic graphs
problems.question: How many intersections have y=−x³ and y=−1/x³?
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Equating them with x≠0 gives x⁶=1.
steps: The only real roots are x=±1. Each gives a valid distinct graph point.

problems.title: Equilateral area from a radius difference
problems.question: An equilateral triangle’s circumradius minus inradius is1. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: For an equilateral triangle,R=2r.

problems.title: A weighted sum of two vectors
problems.question: |a|=2,|b|=1,their angle120°. Find|2a+3b|.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Squared norm=4|a|²+9|b|²+12|a||b|cos120°.

problems.title: A trapezoid area from base triangles
problems.question: Diagonals create triangles at the two trapezoid bases with areas4 and9. Find total area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The two remaining triangle areas are each√(4·9)=6.

problems.question: A=(−4,−3),B=(2,5),centroid M=(−1,2). Find C.

problems.title: Area ratio of two altitude feet
problems.question: In ABC,BD and CE are altitudes. Find area ADE divided by area ABC if A=30°.

problems.title: Convert speed to a three-minute distance
problems.question: How many meters does a car cover in3 minutes at72 km/h?
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: 72 km/h=72000/3600=20 m/s;3 minutes=180 seconds.

problems.title: A two-digit number with two division remainders
problems.question: A two-digit number divided by its digit sum gives quotient4,remainder3;divided by its digit product gives quotient3,remainder5. Find it.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Let tens digit a,units b. Then10a+b=4(a+b)+3 and10a+b=3ab+5.
steps: The first gives b=2a−1. Substitute into the second:6a²−15a+6=0.
Its roots are a=2 or1/2;only a=2 is a digit. Then b=3.
Check:23=4·5+3=3·6+5,with both remainders smaller than the divisors.

problems.title: A tangent and a vector dot product
problems.question: At A=(1,2) on y=2√x,a tangent meets the x-axis at B. Find AB·OA.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Derivative=1/√x,so tangent at1 is y−2=x−1.
steps: Its x-intercept is B=(−1,0). Thus AB=(−2,−2),OA=(1,2).

problems.title: A horizontal chord and an undefined label
problems.question: Line y=b meets y=x²−4x+9 at A,C. The source asks for AB=10 although B is not defined. Find the intended b.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Complete the square:y=(x−2)²+5. A horizontal chord at height b≥5 has length2√(b−5).
steps: Interpreting AB as the intersection chord AC,set2√(b−5)=10.
problems.note: B is undefined in the printed question. The calculation assumes AB is a typo for AC;literally,the condition cannot be evaluated.

problems.title: Overlap of two circles centered at hypotenuse endpoints
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse2 cm and acute angle30°. Circles centered at the hypotenuse endpoints pass through the right-angle vertex. Find overlap area.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The circle radii are triangle legs1 and√3;center distance2. At either intersection,the triangle of centers has angles60°,30°,90°.
steps: The two overlap sectors have central angles120° in the radius1 circle and60° in the radius√3 circle.
Subtract the two congruent center-intersection triangles,whose combined area is√3.

problems.title: Two meetings of a car and cyclist
problems.question: A car and cyclist leave opposite endpoints toward each other. The car reaches the far endpoint,turns,and catches the cyclist2 hours after their first meeting. At the second meeting,the cyclist has covered2/5 of the full distance. How long after the first meeting does the cyclist reach the other endpoint?
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: Let full distance D,cyclist speed u,car speed ku. Before the first meeting,the cyclist covers D/(k+1).
steps: Between meetings,the cyclist covers2D/5−D/(k+1),and the car covers2D/5+D/(k+1). Their time is2 hours.
Taking the ratio k gives k[2/5−1/(k+1)]=2/5+1/(k+1),so(2/5)(k−1)=1 and k=7/2.
After the first meeting,the cyclist has7D/9 left;time=(7/9)/(4/45).

problems.title: Five symmetric roots in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Find a such that x(x¹²−ax⁶+a⁴)=0 has five distinct real roots forming an arithmetic progression.
problems.idea: Apply the formula below and check the result against the stated conditions.
formulas: The nonzero roots occur in opposite pairs. Five such arithmetic roots must be−2r,−r,0,r,2r for r>0.
steps: Set t=x⁶. Its two positive roots must be r⁶ and64r⁶. By Vieta,a=65r⁶>0 and a⁴=64r¹².
Substitute r⁶=a/65:a⁴=64a²/65². Since a>0,this gives a=8/65.
Conversely,this value gives positive t roots in ratio64,so their real sixth roots have ratio2 and produce exactly the stated five-term progression.
